Create a model

Ollama Modelfile Example

Save a recipe with FROM, then run ollama create your-model -f ./Modelfile. Use an installed model tag or a path to your GGUF file. After editing a recipe, rerun ollama create and check ollama show --modelfile your-model to confirm Ollama saved the changes.

  1. Create from an installed model
  2. Import a local GGUF
  3. Check saved and running settings
  4. Fix a failed create or a stale setting

Where are you starting?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Create a model from an installed tag

Start with a tag that appears in ollama list. Replace scratch-base:latest below with that exact tag. If you have a GGUF file, import it as the base model first. Choose a new output name so your existing tag remains available. For first-time setup, follow the Ollama setup guide.

FROM scratch-base:latest
PARAMETER num_ctx 2048
PARAMETER temperature 0
SYSTEM Answer in one short sentence.

Save the text as Modelfile in your current directory and run:

ollama create my-notes:latest -f ./Modelfile
ollama show --modelfile my-notes:latest
ollama run my-notes:latest

The output of show should include the context and system text you set. Changes to SYSTEM and PARAMETER configure the model at runtime. In the local test, the derived and base tags referenced the same weight blob.

Import a GGUF file with a Modelfile

Keep your trusted GGUF file and recipe together. Replace the filename in the example with the actual file name. A relative GGUF path is resolved from the Modelfile’s directory. In our test, the command succeeded even when the shell was in a different directory.

FROM ./qwen.gguf
ollama create scratch-base:latest -f ./recipes/Base.Modelfile
ollama list

In that example, the two files are recipes/Base.Modelfile and recipes/qwen.gguf. For a split GGUF, the official import reference documents listing each shard or using a pattern that matches all original shards. The test here used a single file.

Check what Ollama saved and what it loaded

  1. Use ollama show --modelfile my-notes:latest to review the recipe Ollama saved. For reuse on another machine, keep your original recipe. The generated FROM can point at a blob path local to the current store.
  2. When changing a saved default, edit the original recipe and run ollama create again with the same custom tag. In an isolated check, stop only that test tag before loading the new configuration.
  3. After a request, run ollama ps or read context_length for the tag in /api/ps. A client can send options.num_ctx and load a different context for its request. See how to set and verify the request context.

If create fails or settings stay the same

The base is missing
Check the exact tag in ollama list using the same local server where you run create. If you intended to import a file, check the GGUF relative to the recipe path or use an absolute path. A missing relative file produced invalid model name on the tested version.
A listed :local tag triggers a registry pull
In Ollama 0.40.18, a base imported as scratch-alternate:local appeared in the listing, but using it in FROM made Ollama look for scratch-alternate:latest in the registry. The same fixture worked with :v1. If you see this behavior, try a regular tag such as :v1 and check that it appears locally before rebuilding.
The saved recipe still has the old value
Check the filename passed to -f and the custom output tag. Editing the text file alone left the original setting unchanged in our test. Rebuild that tag and check it again with show.
The running context differs from the saved value
Check the loaded tag and any context override in your client. For a controlled test, send a fresh native request with only the options you intend to use. Estimate the memory impact of a larger context before trying it.

Tested results and sources

On November 28, 2026, we used Ollama 0.40.18 on an Apple Silicon Mac, a separate local server and a Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M GGUF. We verified the saved system text and the shared weight digest. The running context was 2,048 before rebuilding, 4,096 after rebuilding, and 8,192 with a request-level override. Those runs verify configuration and loading.

Download the local observations. See the Ollama Modelfile reference for template and parameter definitions.
